title: Route policy contracts and sanity gates
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures a pragmatic configuration contract for request routing policies, the minimal validation rules we run in the control plane, and a recommended rollout / canary checklist for multi-region deployments. The aim is a small, testable schema + fast validation that prevents common production misconfigurations (e.g., unreachable fallbacks, circular dependencies, missing region mappings).

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to the control-plane routing layer that decides model variant / region / capacity tier selection for incoming inference requests.
- Does NOT cover runtime autoscaler behavior or GPU affinity (those are separate concerns).
- Configuration is authored as JSON or YAML documents stored in config repo; this doc focuses on the contract and safety gates prior to promotion.

High level design goals:
- Explicit, versioned policies with a stable contract so consumers (console, SDKs) can confidently render previews.
- Fast static validation for syntactic and semantic correctness before any deploy.
- Runtime checks (canaries, traffic shadowing) to detect behavior mismatches between control plane preview and data-plane routing.
- Fail-safe defaults and automatic fallback chains to avoid hard outages on misroute.

Minimal routing-policy schema (informal):
- id: stable policy id (string)
- version: semver string (e.g., 1.2.0)
- created_by: author name/email
- description: free text
- match: list of match-clauses (AND semantics between entries in same policy)
- actions: ordered list of actions (route, split, fallback, redirect)
- region_map: mapping logical regions to region groups (used by match/eval)
- guards: runtime constraints (max_latency_ms, credentials_required, cost_tier)
- expiration: optional RFC3339 timestamp after which policy is disabled

Example JSON snippet (as a single-line friendly example in the doc):
{
  "id": "policy:route:v1:search-precise",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "created_by": "priya.nair@redwood.ai",
  "description": "Prefer low-latency model in us-west for short queries, fallback to general model in us-east",
  "match": [
    { "type": "header_contains", "key": "x-client-features", "value": "search:precise" },
    { "type": "max_tokens", "lte": 256 }
  ],
  "actions": [
    { "type": "route", "target": "model:rwkv-2:quant:us-west", "weight": 80 },
    { "type": "route", "target": "model:rwkv-2:quant:us-east", "weight": 15 },
    { "type": "fallback", "target": "model:rwkv-2:cpu:global" }
  ],
  "region_map": { "us": ["us-west", "us-east"] },
  "guards": { "max_latency_ms": 200 },
  "expiration": "2025-12-31T23:59:59Z"
}

Validation checklist (control-plane pre-commit):
1) Schema validation: fields present, types correct, semver on version.
2) Referential checks: each action.target must resolve to a known model variant id in the model registry. If model id unknown -> fail fast.
3) No orphaned fallbacks: every route chain must terminate with a fallback that is routable to at least one healthy regional pool or a defined global pool.
4) Region consistency: region_map keys referenced in matches or actions must exist in infra region config.
5) No circular fallbacks: detect and reject cycles in fallback chains.
6) Guard sanity: numeric guards within allowed limits (e.g., max_latency_ms not negative, cost_tier within [1..5]).
7) Expiration: warn if expiration is missing for short-lived experiments; fail if the expiration is in the past.
8) Canary safety flags: if policy sets weights for traffic split, ensure canary percentage <= 20% unless an explicit override flag is present.
9) Authz: created_by must be part of a team with permission to promote to the intended environment (self-service gating).

Automated tests to run as part of CI pre-promotion:
- Contract tests: unit tests that use a synthetic control plane to assert resolution behavior for canonical inputs (e.g., header + short tokens -> expected target).
- Integration shadow test: shadow 1% of real traffic for 24h and compare latency/cost/percentile success rates against baseline; require no >20% regressions on p95 latency.
- Chaos sanity: simulate one regional pool down and assert policy still reaches a fallback target.

Rollout mechanics (promotion path):
1) Author creates policy in config repo under a feature branch + associated PR with purpose, owner, and intended promotion path.
2) CI runs static validations and contract tests. All checks must pass.
3) Merge to staging config: automatically deploy policy in control-plane staging with 0% active traffic but enabled for shadowing.
4) Shadow interval: run shadow for 24–72 hours (depending on traffic) and run the integration shadow test.
5) Canary ramp strategy: recommended default: 1% -> 5% -> 10% -> 20% each step 30–60 minutes if health metrics stable. Manual gate required before >20%.
6) Observability hooks: confirm per-policy dashboards exist (p50/p95 latency, error rate, cost per 1k tokens, model quality regression metrics if available).
7) Progressive regional enablement: start in single region with highest traffic that matches policy scope, then expand region_map in steps (single region -> region group -> global).
8) Auto rollback triggers: if p95 latency increases >30% or error rate increases >5% absolute vs baseline within a 15-minute window during ramp, rollback automatically to previous config.
9) Post-promote audit: policy author must annotate the promotion with observations and sign-off within 48 hours.

Canary safety best practices (operational):
- Keep canaries small and observable: prefer multiple short ramps rather than one big jump.
- Use synthetic probes that exercise worst-case paths (longest prompts, high concurrency) in addition to user traffic.
- Force periodic drain windows to exercise fallback logic.
- Maintain a canary kill-switch in the console that can immediately disable the policy or force traffic to fallback.

Sample validation regexes and quick checks (to include in validator):
- id: ^[a-z0-9:_-]{5,64}$
- version: ^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$
- expiration: ISO8601 / RFC3339 check
- guard cost_tier: integer in [1,5]
- weight sums: for actions of type route the sum(weights) <= 100; if sum < 100 must have fallback present.

Operational runbook snippets (for on-call SRE):
- Symptom: Traffic dropped for a region after policy promotion -> Check recent policy promotions for overlapping region_map edits and evaluate fallback availability.
- Quick mitigation: disable the policy in control-plane and revert to previous config; if control-plane UI is unavailable, mark the policy as disabled via the admin API.
- Diagnosing circular fallback: call the resolve API with a minimal request and inspect the returned resolution path; if it loops, identify the policy ids in path and revert the most recent change.

Open items for follow-up (TODOs):
- Decide canonical location and ownership for the model registry resolver used during pre-commit referential checks (who runs the resolver, cache TTL).
- Add automated quality checks that compute similarity/regression for generation quality when switching model families (requires eval harness integration).
- Define exact thresholds for metric-based auto rollback (current numbers are proposals).

References and links:
- GH PR for control-plane resolver: GITHUB-PR-4982
- Staging dashboard template: CONFLUENCE-PLAT-2345
- Jira Epic for routing policy rollout automation: JIRA-PLT-1021

Notes to reviewers:
This is intentionally short and operational. Aim: keep the policy contract minimal so the validator can run quickly in CI and still catch the majority of high-risk mistakes. Feedback wanted on: additional semantic checks we should add, sensible defaults for the canary ramp durations, and whether a hard 20% canary cap should be a policy or just a recommended guard.
